clue.text: The morning star that glows in the dark

blocks.note: first meaning: the poetic name for Venus seen before dawn
second meaning: a substance that gives off light after being energised

explanation.surface: A bright planet at dawn that also seems to shine at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves look like one description of a star; they are two separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both Venus as harbinger of dawn (poetic, from Greek light-bringer) and any luminescent coating material.

clue.text: Tube annoyance? Better to shun termini

indicators.note: shunning the termini means dropping both end letters of the word

blocks.note: British idiom: something that gives you the pip annoys you
better without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Annoyed by the Underground, someone decides to avoid the terminal stations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' and 'termini' suggest London trains; the tube is a laboratory one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipette is a slender glass tube used in laboratories to measure and transfer small volumes of liquid.

clue.text: Musical pieces being the making of poetaster?

indicators.note: making something out of raw material reshapes it, so the letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: a poetaster is a feeble, would-be poet

explanation.surface: A second-rate versifier made his name writing light stage works.
explanation.walkthrough: A poetaster is a writer of trashy verse; 'the making of' sounds like a career break.
explanation.definitionFit: Operettas are short, light operas with spoken dialogue, works for the musical stage like Gilbert and Sullivan.

clue.text: Qualification for victory on one's round

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
V for victory
one's read as one is, with one as I: I is, with the apostrophe treated as a contraction of is
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Earning the right to win depends on your lap of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as I + S, the S standing for is in the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition or stipulation attached to an agreement, the sense of qualification as a limiting clause.

clue.text: See honours taking precedence in gross manner

blocks.note: OBEs are British honours, Officers of the Order of the British Empire
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a classic crossword one

explanation.surface: Look at medals being given priority over everything else, grossly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking precedence' tells you the honours come first, ahead of the see. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Obesely means in a grossly fat way, gross here in its sense of overweight or bloated.

clue.text: Old Greek writer to exhaust Greek character endlessly with love

indicators.note: without an end, the Greek letter loses its final letter

blocks.note: to sap is to drain or exhaust
PHI, a letter of the Greek alphabet, cut short
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Reading an ancient Greek author leaves you worn out, yet fond of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho was the lyric poet of Lesbos in the sixth century BC, an ancient Hellenic author.

clue.text: Second-class with regard to love? That'll make you hardened

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
CL is a standard abbreviation for class
erotic means concerning sexual love

explanation.surface: Being treated as second-rate in romance will make a person cynical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-class' looks like one unit, but it splits into two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Sclerotic is the medical word for tissues or arteries that have become rigid, extended to mean set in its ways.

clue.text: Food for thought in book accepted by apostle with some hesitation

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the book abbreviation goes inside the apostle

blocks.note: Saint Paul, the apostle to the Gentiles
B is short for book
um, a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Spiritual nourishment from a scripture that the apostle took up only hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food for thought' reads as a phrase in the surface, but it is the whole definition, with food here meaning nourishment for the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pabulum literally means nourishment, and is used figuratively of material that feeds the mind.

clue.text: Any loch, when stormy, may become calm

indicators.note: a storm churns the water, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters of any and loch

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake whipped up by a gale can settle to stillness afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A loch is a Scottish lake. The kingfisher (halcyon) was fabled to calm the sea while it nested.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon describes idyllically peaceful weather or days, from the legend of the kingfisher stilling waves.

clue.text: Friend embraces female -- a sign of great significance?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the friend word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
a hen is a female bird
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A friend hugging a woman might be read as a momentous portent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sign of great significance' reads as one phrase, but 'a sign' is wordplay and only the last three words define.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phenomenal is extraordinary or remarkable, so it carries great weight; the question mark flags a loose fit.

clue.text: Score with a pike

blocks.note: first meaning: a tally or account owed, as at a restaurant
second meaning: an old long-handled weapon with a hooked blade

explanation.surface: An angler notching up a catch of one large fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The pike looks like the fish, but here it is the weapon; a bill was a halberd-type pole arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an amount owed, which a restaurant presents as the tab; the bill was also a medieval infantry pole weapon.

clue.text: Easy time in a famous mother's biography

blocks.note: first meaning: a carefree, comfortable existence
second meaning: the story of Old Mother Riley, a music-hall and film character

explanation.surface: Reading a celebrity mum's memoir makes for a relaxing spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Riley was a comic Irish washerwoman played in drag by Arthur Lucan in British variety and films of the 1930s-50s.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a life of luxury and ease without worries, and literally names an account of Riley's career.

clue.text: Hospital department has poor-quality, unusable energy source

definitions.note: a loose definition: the term measures energy unavailable for work

blocks.note: ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
British informal for shoddy or in poor condition

explanation.surface: A hospital unit with shoddy kit that wastes its power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Ropy is British slang for poor or unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: In thermodynamics this quantity measures the disorder of a system, the part of its heat that cannot do work.

clue.text: A great many favouring merger

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
a fusion is a merging together

explanation.surface: Lots of people backing the joining of two companies.
explanation.definitionFit: A profusion is an abundance or large quantity of something, so it stands for a lot of things.

clue.text: Staying-power - it protects opera hero endlessly

indicators.note: what protects something surrounds it, so the word for it goes around the rest
without an end, the hero's name loses its final letter

blocks.note: it in crosswordese is sex appeal, abbreviated SA
Tamino, the prince in Mozart's The Magic Flute, cut short

explanation.surface: Endurance shields a tenor lead from collapse throughout the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a classic convention; TAMIN goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the physical and mental endurance to keep going, a direct synonym for staying-power.

clue.text: I'm  the thing a vet treated, nursing one like an ape

indicators.note: treated, as by a doctor, suggests the letters are worked on and changed
nursing means cradling in one's arms, so the treated letters hold the numeral

blocks.note: taken as written
it is the thing
taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sick animal speaks: it is the creature a vet looked after, tending a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A VET is rearranged to AT VE, then I goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to copy, so imitative, meaning given to copying others, describes ape-like mimicry.

clue.text: Girl, one working in religious outpost

blocks.note: a miss is a girl
the Roman numeral for one
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A young woman labouring at a remote church station.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is a settlement where missionaries live and preach, often a remote base far from home.

clue.text: One gets caught and left imprisoned in a naked state

definitions.note: a past participle for a verb answer: the clue uses the old sense of the verb, to shut in

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the two abbreviations go inside the state

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
nude means naked
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
L is short for left

explanation.surface: A prisoner is arrested and left locked up without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: C and L go inside NUDE, after I. The definition is weak: the verb's archaic sense is to enclose or confine.
explanation.definitionFit: Include once meant to shut in or confine, as a prisoner is enclosed within walls.

clue.text: Too much swell to moor?

blocks.note: surface reading: the sea is running too high for a boat to tie up
setter's reading: an excess, with the word for breaking waves at its start

explanation.surface: Waves too big for a boat to come alongside the quay.
explanation.walkthrough: Swell here means the heaving sea, and the word for it begins the answer; the whole thing describes overabundance.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an excessive amount of something, an overabundance that cloys.

clue.text: Climbing around, wearing injury support

indicators.note: something worn has a body inside it, so the support goes around the abbreviation

blocks.note: a sling supports an injured arm
ca. is short for circa, around

explanation.surface: A climber clambering about with an arm in a sling.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaling a wall or peak means ascending it, a straightforward synonym for climbing up.

clue.text: Cork perhaps needed for the main drink

blocks.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A cork is needed to seal the bottle holding the principal beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like a bottle stopper, but it is the harbour city in southern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is an Irish city with a large natural harbour, an example of a coastal town with docks.

clue.text: Area featured in American A-to-Z?

blocks.note: surface reading: a district shown in a US street atlas
setter's reading: a US state whose two-letter postal code is literally A then Z

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood marked in a street guide of an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-to-Z is a British book of street maps. The state's postal abbreviation is AZ, which runs from A to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a south-western US state, officially abbreviated AZ by the postal service.

clue.text: Without a horse, lethargy can develop in a big way

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the slang letter is taken out
developing means growing into something new, so the remaining letters change form

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
taken as written before the removal

explanation.surface: Deprived of their mount, a rider becomes enormously sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse as slang for heroin gives H, which is removed before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatly means to a large extent or degree, an adverb matching the phrase hugely or considerably.

clue.text: Can magic and virtue possibly fill forty minutes in M.S.N.D.?

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters might come out in some other order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters of can, magic and virtue

explanation.surface: Wondering whether stage magic and goodness could pad out a Shakespeare performance.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck boasts: 'I'll put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes.' 'and' joins can and magic to virtue but is not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail or fly round the globe is what Puck promises to accomplish in forty minutes in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Underground supplier of Australian beer

blocks.note: first meaning: the London metro system
second meaning: Australian slang for a can of beer

explanation.surface: A secret source bootlegging lager from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground supplier' reads like an illicit dealer; the first word stands alone as London's subway, and Australians call a can of beer a tube.
explanation.definitionFit: Londoners call their rail network by this nickname, while Australians use it for a tinny holding lager.

clue.text: Old journal by Irish leader that is about a political visionary

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is used
about means surrounding, so the Latin abbreviation goes round the rest

blocks.note: id est, Latin for that is, normally written i.e.
O is a standard abbreviation for old
a log is a journal or record
the first letter of Irish

explanation.surface: An old Dublin magazine profiling a statesman with grand ideals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' gives the full Latin ID EST, not just IE; O, LOG and I sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideologist devises or champions a doctrine of political ideas, a theorist with a vision of society.

clue.text: One who cares for the church — Blake, for instance

definitions.text: One who cares for the church

blocks.clueFragment: One who cares for the church
blocks.note: first meaning: the officer who looks after a church building and graveyard
second meaning: first name of a fictional British detective

explanation.surface: A church caretaker, perhaps the poet William Blake.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake suggests the poet, but Sexton Blake was a detective hero of British story papers and pulp fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton maintains a parish church and its graveyard; Sexton Blake is a long-running fictional sleuth.

clue.text: Get to retreat during erratic military planning

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the word runs backwards
during means within, so the turned word sits inside the other

blocks.note: stray means wandering or erratic
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops are told to pull back amid chaotic battle tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' and 'military' share a war picture, but retreat only turns the first word round; 'erratic' gives a word meaning wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: Strategy is the art of planning a campaign as a whole, originally the general's craft in warfare.
